ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *grěti, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰer- (“warm”). Cognate with Ancient Greek θερμός (thermós, “warm”) (whence те́рмос (térmos), термо- (termo-)), Latin formus, furnus, and possibly Proto-Germanic *warmaz (whence English warm).

Borrowed from New Latin Eurōpaeismus, from Europae(us) (“European”) + -ismus (“-ism”), with both elements borrowed from Ancient Greek Εὐρωπαῖος (Eurōpaîos) and -ισμός (-ismós) respectively. The expected result in Latin, however, is *Eurōpaismus. Compare Greek ευρωπαϊσμός (evropaïsmós). Compare also Latin borrowings from Ancient Greek such as Iūdaismus (“Judaism”).
